title: Financial accounting
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Record business transactions with double-entry bookkeeping, adjust and close the books, and prepare and read the income statement, balance sheet, statement of changes in equity and cash flow statement, including revenue recognition, receivables, inventory, long-lived assets, liabilities and equity.
primary_reading: OpenStax Principles of Accounting, Volume 1: Financial Accounting (free)

weeks.1: The role of accounting and the accounting equation
weeks.2: Recording transactions: debits, credits and journals
weeks.4: The financial statements and closing the books
weeks.6: Inventory: FIFO, LIFO and weighted average
weeks.9: Equity: stock, dividends and retained earnings
weeks.11: Internal control and ethics in reporting

blocks.deliverable: Prepare all four statements for a small business.
Compute cost of goods sold three ways.
Week 7 midterm; build a depreciation schedule.
Prepare a cash flow statement by the indirect method.
Find ten key numbers in a public company 10-K.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Bookkeeping practice set: record three months of transactions for a small company, make the adjusting entries, prepare and reconcile the four financial statements, and write a one-page memo explaining the company's results and cash position.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
